title: Sparse local adaptation + latency budgeting for cross-encoder upgrades (multilingual)
creator: Leah Martinez
description:
Background: Our current strategy for improving rerank quality in non-English locales has been to evaluate larger cross-encoder variants, but those come with significant P95/P99 latency and cost regressions. This ticket explores a hybrid approach: small, locale-specific sparse adapters (adapter-style finetunes) applied to a compact cross-encoder backbone + explicit per-request latency budgeting and a staged canary rollout to minimize customer impact.

Goals: (1) Improve per-locale rerank quality (nDCG@10 and MRR uplift) compared to the baseline compact cross-encoder without adapters. (2) Keep median and P95 token-generation latency within a defined budget so production SLAs are not violated. (3) Provide a deterministic upgrade path (canary, staged rollouts, automatic fallback) and automated regression checks integrated into the rerank regression harness.

Scope: prototype sparse-adapter training recipes for 6 priority locales (en-US, es-ES, fr-FR, de-DE, pt-BR, ja-JP), integrate adapter loading into the rerank endpoint, implement a latency budget validator and canary routing policy in the serving runtime, and add locale-specific evals to the regression suite.

Non-goals: full monolithic retraining of base cross-encoder weights, multi-locale adapters in this phase, or persistent changes to batching logic beyond small heuristics for early-exit under high-load.
acceptance_criteria: Adapters: Locale adapter artifacts produced for 6 locales and stored in model-catalog with metadata (size, float16/quantization info).
Quality: Mean nDCG@10 uplift >= 4% over compact baseline per locale on the held-out eval set; no locale shows >1% degradation.
Latency: P50 latency increase <= 10ms and P95 <= 35ms against baseline compact cross-encoder for 16-token queries under production-like load. P99 must remain < 120ms for single-request path.
Regression checks: New locale eval suites run in CI with clear fail/pass thresholds; failing canary blocks rollout.
Rollout: Implemented canary routing with automatic rollback on quality regressions or latency SLO breaches documented in the runbook.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Leah Martinez: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded. Decided to prioritize adapter approach over full re-training to limit deployment complexity. Action: Omar to draft training recipe and schedule a 2-day fine-tune run. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RER/Locale+Sparse+Adapters

2026-02-25 - Omar Singh: Initial adapter recipe (LoRA-style) implemented; trained 3 small adapters on synthetic locales dataset. Preliminary eval shows +5.2% nDCG@10 on es-ES and +3.6% on fr-FR. Noted P95 latency +28ms on test rig. Logged results to dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/rerank/locale-adapter/exp-27518

2026-03-01 - Priya Anand (PM): Requested explicit latency budget per-tier. We agreed: "gold" customers get canary + wider rollout; "standard" customers see adapters off by default until canary passes. Action: add tagging in routing policy and documentation in Console route settings.

2026-03-04 - Omar Singh: Implemented a lightweight latency budget validator in the serving runtime that estimates added per-request cost of loading adapters and signals if the request would exceed configured threshold. Unit tests added. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/1423
2026-03-07 - Design review: Megan Cho reviewed UX for Console toggle enabling per-route locale-adapter usage. Minor copy suggestions made. UX stub: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1abcUXdesign

2026-03-09 - SRE (Carlos Vega): Load test with autoscaling shows stable throughput but increased memory pressure on 8GB GPU hosts when multiple locales are warmed simultaneously. Proposed mitigation: limit concurrent adapter warmstarts per host and prioritize KV warm cache reuse. Added as follow-up: ENG-27902.
